Site Spawner — Wave 7: the node-slot SSR runtime target

Status: DECIDED — building 6 slices (D61–D72). Opened at Strategize 2026-07-15. Epic: bp-cloud-site-spawner-epic. Charter at D60; this wave opens D61+. Prior waves W1–W6 (static-Astro spine, publish→auto-rebuild, Cloudflare-in-front) are DONE and live-proven on guerrilla.

The wish (verbatim intent)

The static deploy pipeline is PROVEN PERFECT (Astro: create→6-stages→live→rollback, publish→auto-rebuild, CF-in-front, self-healing). Now unlock the SECOND class of the founding vision: CONTAINER frameworks (Next.js first, then nuxt/sveltekit) via the NODE-SLOT SSR RUNTIME TARGET — the "second serve-backend" the founding architecture named ("ONE deploy state machine, TWO runtime targets: static-symlink-swap OR node-slot SSR"). Today only static-symlink-swap exists; container frameworks (site.framework in @container_frameworks ~w(nextjs nuxt sveltekit)) have nowhere to run.

Deliver the node-slot backend: a per-site long-running Node SSR process (next start / node server.js) that the SAME 6-stage machine drives — PLAN(build_id) → BUILD(npm ci && npm run build, container output not a static dist/) → STAGE(immutable release) → HEALTH(curl the RUNNING node process, not a static file) → SWITCH(flip the Caddy upstream to the new slot's node port, blue/green — mirrors instance-deploy.sh's slot mechanism) → RETIRE(stop the old node process, keep N for rollback). The KEY difference from static: the artifact is a running PROCESS with a port + lifecycle (systemd slot unit like barkpark-slot@), health-gated by an HTTP probe to the process, Caddy reverse-proxies to it.

Reuse EVERYTHING proven: the deploy state machine, force-nonce, fail-closed HEALTH, the blue/green slot + Caddy upstream flip (instance-deploy.sh is the template), the provisioning seam (a next-starter template mirroring astro-starter), publish→auto-rebuild, CF-in-front. Ship Next.js as the flagship (a next-starter that fetches Barkpark content + bakes bp-* HEALTH markers, SSR/app router). MUST be: fail-closed, zero-downtime (blue/green), standalone-first (the box runs the node process itself, zero external accounts), resource-bounded (cap the per-site node footprint; document density vs static). END with a LIVE proof on guerrilla: spawn a Next.js site, deploy, watch the 6 stages drive a running node process to a live SSR URL with bp-* markers, then rollback (<1s) to the previous node slot.

Strategic direction for this wave

Ship the node-slot SSR runtime target as a thin, proven foundation — Next.js flagship — driven by the SAME 6-stage machine, and prove it LIVE on guerrilla end to end. This is genuinely NEW architecture: the artifact is a process lifecycle, not a symlink. A bit more PLAN is warranted than the static waves, but stay BUILD-oriented: a thin node-slot engine + a next-starter + a live guerrilla proof, not a design deck.

The central architectural fork the survey MUST settle

There are TWO pieces of prior art that both claim "run a container framework," and they are NOT the same mechanism:

  • Path A — the existing Go Docker runtime (internal/runtime/runtime.go). Already implements Docker-based blue/green for the pre-W1 kind=container site: PortAllocator (deterministic loopback port range), docker load → docker run on a fresh port → HTTP health-check → render Caddyfile + reload → drain the old container, plus scale-to-zero via a barkpark-waker. It SOLVES port allocation + blue/green + Caddy + cold-start already — but it depends on dockerd and a Docker image builder (D7 called the nixpacks/docker off-box builder "unshipped AND wrong-shaped"), and it does NOT use the 6-stage bash machine, the co-located content-fetch/token plumbing, force-nonce, or fail-closed marker-HEALTH that the static wave proved. Is it live? Almost certainly vestigial (static had "zero live rows ever"; container likely same).
  • Path B — the systemd node-slot the wish names. next start / node server.js as a systemd slot unit (per-site-per-slot template mirroring barkpark-slot@), driven by the SAME 6-stage engine (site-deploy.sh extended with a runtime-target branch, OR a sibling engine sharing the skeleton — mirrors the D11 "don't parameterize instance-deploy.sh" reasoning). Reuses DeployRunner, the provisioner, force-nonce, fail-closed HEALTH, immutable releases/<build_id>/, co-located content fetch. Port allocation + a two-dimensional systemd template + Caddy reverse_proxy flip are net-new but mirror instance-deploy.sh.

I lean HARD toward Path B: the wish explicitly names it ("systemd slot unit like barkpark-slot@", "the SAME 6-stage state machine", "next start / node server.js", "the box runs the node process itself, zero external accounts"). Docker cuts directly against "standalone-first, zero external accounts" and reopens a build-image dependency the static wave deliberately avoided. BUT the Go Docker runtime's PortAllocator and Caddy-render logic are genuine, tested prior art — the survey must decide whether to harvest that logic into the node-slot path or leave it as a separate Docker path. Decide finalizes after two explore rounds.

The choices I lean toward (tentative)

  1. Sibling/branch engine, shared skeleton. The node runtime target has a fundamentally different SWITCH (Caddy reverse_proxy port flip + graceful reload, not symlink rename), HEALTH (probe a live process on its own port, not a throwaway server over dist/), STAGE (Next standalone output — .next/standalone/server.js + .next/static + public, which bundles a minimal node_modules, UNLIKE D8's dist-only), and RETIRE (stop a process, not rm a dir). It SHARES the state-machine shape, BPSTAGE protocol, flock serialize, force-nonce, PLAN idempotency, fail-closed HEALTH, and the immutable releases layout.
  2. Two-dimensional systemd template unit — barkpark-slot@ is single-instance (blue/green for ONE box). Sites need per-site AND per-slot: e.g. barkpark-site@<slug>-<blue|green>.service reading .sites/<slug>/.slots/<slot>.env (node PORT + release dir), ExecStart runs the standalone server from releases/<build_id>/.
  3. Per-site-per-slot port allocator — instance-deploy uses fixed 4000/4001. Sites need a dynamic range (e.g. 4100–4999) allocated deterministically, persisted (the sites.port column ALREADY EXISTS; the Go DefaultPortAllocator already picks lowest-free in a range) and collision-free across many sites × two slots.
  4. Caddy upstream = per-site reverse_proxy to the live slot port. Mirror the static path-handle (D4) but reverse_proxy localhost:<slot-port> instead of file_server. SWITCH rewrites the port + graceful reload (the instance-deploy port-flip awk/sed is the template). The Go caddyfile renderer ALREADY emits reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:<port> for container sites — real scaffolding to reuse.
  5. Rollback = keep the previous slot WARM. "<1s rollback" + "keep N for rollback": if the previous node slot stays running, rollback is a pure Caddy port flip (<1s, no reboot). That trades RAM for instant rollback — document the density cost. (Alternative: stop old, re-boot on rollback ~seconds — violates the <1s bar. Survey settles.)
  6. Resource caps + density doctrine. systemd MemoryMax/CPUQuota per site (the BUILD path already uses systemd-run --scope, D7). A static site ≈ 16K on disk + 0 RAM; a warm Next process ≈ 80–150MB resident. Cap each and document how many sites fit guerrilla's headroom.
  7. Next.js flagship template — next-starter mirroring astro-starter: output: 'standalone', a Barkpark content-fetch lib (reuse @barkpark/core; mind the findOne-throws-on-empty gotcha, D40), a Base layout baking bp-build-id/bp-content-rev/bp-doc-id markers SSR-side (app router, in the rendered HTML). Provisioner needs a framework→template switch (today hardcoded to templates/astro-starter).
  8. Fail-closed + zero-downtime — build+boot the new node slot, health-probe it on ITS port, ONLY flip Caddy after green; unhealthy new slot → stop it, old keeps serving. This is exactly instance-deploy's proven pattern.
  9. NEW security surface: request-time tenant code. D12 noted static is build-time-only (no isolation crux). A node SSR process runs tenant code CONTINUOUSLY at request time. Bound it this wave with systemd hardening (NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectSystem=strict, DynamicUser?, resource caps); defer full multi-tenant sandboxing but name the threat model.

The survey plan (this wave's scout fleet)

Width is cheap now. Each surveyor answers one broad question with evidence from the repo, the deploy scripts, and bp papers/tasks. The Digest phase distills into a verify plan.

  1. site-deploy-anatomy — Full anatomy of deploy/site-deploy.sh: every stage function, what is reusable verbatim (flock, force-nonce, BPSTAGE emit, PLAN idempotency, releases/<build_id> layout) vs static-specific (symlink swap SWITCH, throwaway-server HEALTH, dist-only STAGE). Where would a RUNTIME_TARGET branch slot in vs a sibling site-deploy-node.sh? Why: decides branch-vs-sibling — the biggest engineering call.
  2. instance-deploy-slot-mechanism — Deep-dive the blue/green template: .slots/<slot>.env generation, PORT override, the health-gate loop, the Caddy port-flip awk/sed, .slots/<slot>.sha rollback, graceful reload. Map EVERY mechanism to node-slot reuse. Why: this is the literal template the wish names.
  3. go-docker-runtime (Path A) — Fully map internal/runtime/runtime.go: PortAllocator range + collision logic, docker blue/green, Caddy render+reload, drainContainer, barkpark-waker scale-to-zero, healthCheck. Is it LIVE anywhere (any real deployment row / prod caddy block)? Does it need dockerd + a Docker image builder that isn't shipped? Why: settles whether we harvest its port/Caddy logic or leave Docker as a dead path.
  4. systemd-template-semantics — Can a systemd template %i encode two dimensions (slug+slot)? EnvironmentFile path templating, enable/disable/restart lifecycle for MANY per-site units, any multi-instance template prior art in deploy/systemd/. Hardening directives available (NoNewPrivileges, DynamicUser, MemoryMax, ProtectSystem). Why: the per-site node process lifecycle rests on this.
  5. port-allocation — What is sites.port used for today (registry/deployment)? Any existing box-side or cloud-side port allocator? What port range is free on guerrilla (what's bound now)? How does the Go container path assign + persist ports, and can node-slot reuse it deterministically across sites × slots? Why: the crux — deterministic, collision-free, recoverable port assignment.
  6. caddy-reverse-proxy-render — How the Go caddyfile.go/runtime.go renders a reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:<port> block for a container Site (mergeSite), where the port is sourced, how it interacts with W6 TLSMode, and whether a bash Caddy port-flip (instance-deploy style) or the Go renderer owns the node-slot upstream. Why: SWITCH mechanism + who owns the Caddy mutation.
  7. deployrunner-dispatch — How DeployRunner.start_run/2 builds the site-deploy command, passes build_id + the BUILD_ALLOW scrubbed env, and where a kind/runtime-target signal would branch static vs node. Does the relay (/v1/admin/site-deploy, box_relay, cloud deploy.ex) carry kind/framework to the box? Why: how the CP tells the box "this is a node deploy."
  8. provisioner-and-next-starter — How provisioner.ex materializes astro-starter (framework→template mapping, currently hardcoded); what a next-starter needs (next.config standalone, package.json, content-fetch lib, Base layout SSR markers). Where the framework switch lands. Why: the provisioning seam for the flagship template.
  9. astro-starter-reuse — Anatomy of templates/astro-starter/: build-time content fetch over the scoped public-read route, the 5 bp-* markers, the token flow. What is reusable for next-starter (content-fetch lib, marker names, token env) vs Astro-specific. Why: don't reinvent the content/marker plumbing.
  10. barkpark-core-ssr — The @barkpark/core / JS SDK content-fetch lib astro uses: can it run at SSR REQUEST time (server component / getServerSideProps) not just build time? Does it need the read token at runtime (env)? The findOne-throws-on-empty gotcha (D40) and how a Next SSR page fails-closed on empty content. Why: SSR fetches at request time — a new runtime path for the SDK.
  11. next-standalone-output — Next.js output: 'standalone' artifact shape (.next/standalone/server.js, .next/static, public, bundled minimal node_modules). What STAGE must copy into releases/<build_id>/ (contrast D8's dist-only) and the boot command. Version pin + node version on guerrilla (Node 26.5.0 per D7). Why: STAGE + boot correctness for a real Next build.
  12. process-health-gate — The mechanism to boot a node process on a slot port, wait for readiness, curl it, assert 200 + bp-* markers in the SSR-rendered HTML, then EITHER keep it live OR kill it. Contrast static's throwaway server. Does the health-gated process BECOME the serving process (instance-deploy boots-then-gates-in-place model)? Why: HEALTH for a process is the defining difference from static.
  13. rollback-warm-vs-cold — For <1s node rollback: keep the previous slot RUNNING (warm, instant Caddy flip, costs RAM) vs stop-and-reboot (~seconds). How instance-deploy rolls back (reboot idle slot from .sha + flip). RAM cost of N warm slots. Why: the <1s rollback bar depends on this tradeoff.
  14. registry-container-kind — In cloud/: what state a kind=container Site carries (port, scale_mode always_on/zero) that static doesn't, whether the deploy route (deploy_static_site) branches on kind, and whether there is ANY working container deploy flow today or it's vestigial. Framework legality gate (@container_frameworks). Why: the CP schema + route surface for the container path.
  15. cli-container-surface — Does bp cloud site create --framework nextjs --kind container + deploy/rollback/status work today, or only static? What the Go cloudclient carries (kind, framework, runtime target, port) and what's net-new for a node deploy's streamed stages. Why: the product-voice verb surface for the flagship.
  16. resource-density — guerrilla's RAM/CPU headroom, the systemd-run --scope BUILD-cap precedent, per-process Next memory footprint, how many warm node sites fit, and the honest density tradeoff vs static to document. Why: resource-bounded is a MUST; density is the doctrine to write.
  17. prior-art-papers — Search Barkpark papers + tasks for node-slot / SSR / runtime-target / two-serve-backends / port allocator / the founding architecture doc + /papers/choosing-your-site-framework + the backlog task site-spawner-backlog-ssr-target. Any prior design thinking to reconcile. Why: don't re-decide what a prior mind already settled.
  18. ci-merge-reality — Confirm the inherited doc-gates red (chat_live.ex:377) + elixir flakes (QueueTest/OrgRequireMfa/StudioLiveSheetPresence), and which gates gate a change under cloud/ vs deploy/ vs internal/ vs api/ vs templates/. Why: builders must know what red is inherited vs their own.

Wave log (this wave)

Strategize (2026-07-15) — Direction set: ship Path B (systemd node-slot) as a thin proven foundation, Next.js flagship, live proof on guerrilla; harvest the Go PortAllocator/Caddy logic where it fits. 18 surveyors dispatched. Central fork to settle: Go Docker runtime (Path A) vs systemd node-slot (Path B). NEXT: Digest folds surveyor reports + designs the verify fleet.

Survey digest (2026-07-15) — 18 surveyors folded

The central fork is SETTLED by evidence: Path B (systemd node-slot sibling engine), harvest Path A only for logic. Five independent surveyors converge that the Go Docker runtime (internal/runtime/runtime.go) is real, unit-tested, but DEAD on the box — no systemd unit, no Makefile target, no CI reference, buildState always returns an empty LiveSites slice, the off-box image builder was never shipped, and charter D7 already rejected it. Harvest only the DefaultPortAllocator lowest-free-in-range algorithm and the Caddy render→reload→drain sequencing; do NOT extend Path A, and do NOT reuse its /v1/agent/* routes or Deployment.image_tag column (a disjoint, abandoned deployment-identity model).

Established (well-anchored, cross-confirmed)

  • Engine shape: a NEW sibling deploy/site-deploy-node.sh mirroring D11's own precedent (do NOT parameterize site-deploy.sh/instance-deploy.sh). BUT extract the shared primitives into deploy/lib/site-deploy-common.sh — emit()/BPSTAGE is a HARD wire contract (cloud/.../sites/deploy.ex:772 hardcodes the regex over exactly PLAN|BUILD|STAGE|HEALTH|SWITCH|RETIRE), and with_caddy_lock is already a two-writer contract whose duplication caused a real lost-update bug once — a third writer must JOIN the lock, not copy-paste it.
  • STAGE inverts D8: Next output:'standalone' = three copies into releases/<build_id>/ (.next/standalone/ + .next/static/ + public/) and it BUNDLES node_modules — unlike static's dist-only doctrine. Empirically confirmed against a real Next 16.2.4 build. Boot = PORT=<p> node server.js (server.js honors PORT/HOSTNAME env).
  • HEALTH = boot-in-place then gate, NOT static's throwaway probe. Both process-lifecycle precedents (instance-deploy.sh + runtime.go) boot the REAL artifact on its REAL port, gate it there, and only then flip Caddy. D11's own stated reason for static's throwaway model ("no process to boot/restart") is exactly the condition node-slot does not meet. Must assert bp-* markers BY VALUE (D26 content-truth), not the Go runtime's weaker any-non-5xx. Exit code 14 = HEALTH-failed is the cross-engine convention.
  • SWITCH = Caddy reverse_proxy port-flip under with_caddy_lock → caddy validate → systemctl reload caddy → revert-on-failure, anchored to a PER-SITE block (site-deploy.sh's arm_caddy_site_route pattern), NOT instance-deploy.sh's whole-file sed (safe only because there is one app). The Go renderer's whole-file Render() would silently discard the hand-injected static blocks — bash must own the node upstream mutation.
  • <1s rollback needs a WARM previous slot — genuinely unprecedented: every existing engine STOPS the loser immediately after a flip, and instance-deploy.sh's own --rollback is cold (reboot+health-gate, tens of seconds). Immutable releases/<build_id>/ make a warm-flip safe (no shared-checkout git-reset like instance-deploy). Recommended: 2-tier — 1 warm slot for true <1s, older generations cold.
  • Provisioner materialize is framework-agnostic (atomic partial-rename + marker guard) — reusable verbatim, just feed a different template path. The BARKPARK_* env contract and the 5 bp-* marker names are explicitly cross-framework; reuse verbatim, render SSR-side.
  • Dispatch seam: DeployRunner.command_for/1 branches only on :deploy/:rollback; DeployRequest has no framework/kind field (closed 7-key env allow-list, unknown key → 400). Cloud ALREADY sends framework: site.framework in the payload but the box drops it. Extend with a validated closed-enum field mirroring mode.
  • SSR fetch is a solved path: @barkpark/nextjs already ships request-time SSR fetch; but the thin flagship should use astro-starter's proven simple @barkpark/core one-shot (NOT createPreloader, which leaks request state). Read token lives in the slot's systemd env for the process lifetime, never NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed.

Coverage map — checked-and-FOUND vs checked-and-NOT-FOUND (absences are decisions-in-waiting)

  • FOUND: site-deploy.sh (937L) + instance-deploy.sh full stage anatomy; barkpark-slot@.service (Elixir-specific: MIX_BUILD_ROOT/api/start.sh); @container_frameworks live on main; the Go PortAllocator (7001-7999); D7/D8/D11/D12 charter decisions; cloud→box relay carries framework (dropped box-side); guerrilla live port audit (7001-7999 FREE, only slot@blue running, no dockerd references, only 3 static sites on disk); Next standalone artifact shape (real build).
  • NOT FOUND (net-new, no prior art): deploy/site-deploy-node.sh (zero); templates/next-starter (zero — must be built); a generic 2-dimensional systemd template unit (barkpark-slot@ is Elixir-coupled); any per-site port allocator (Go one has a broken empty-state source); any warm-standby rollback precedent; any systemd HARDENING precedent anywhere (all units run User=root, only one bare MemoryMax); any long-running-process resource cap (only the BUILD-time systemd-run scope).
  • CORNERS NO SURVEYOR FULLY REACHED: real next start boot-to-healthy TIME on guerrilla hardware (never run there); real standalone node_modules SIZE + RSS (pnpm-symlink artifact made the probe unreliable); whether the API returns 404 vs 200+[] for a zero-doc query (the D40 pivot); whether any kind=container Site exists in prod today (backward-compat risk of the kind-naming call); internal/caddyfile/caddyfile.go render internals for a live reverse_proxy flip; self-hosted next start honoring revalidateTag/ISR.

Contradictions + tensions the Decide phase cannot skip

  • D40 (findOne-on-empty) — surveyors DISAGREE, and it MATTERS more for SSR. Two surveys say findOne() returns doc ?? null (no throw); one traces that the underlying docs.ts query executor does NOT catch BarkparkNotFoundError, so if the API 404s an empty-type query (vs 200+[]), it throws uncaught. For static that is a one-time BUILD fail; for SSR it is a per-request 500 with no last-good net — directly threatening the fail-closed promise. Must be RUN to settle whether the flagship needs a core patch or a defensive catch THIS wave.
  • The name "container" is already spoken-for. kind=="container" is the schema DEFAULT and already routes to the legacy off-box builder; the deploy router branches EXACTLY on kind=="static" vs else, rollback 422s for non-static, content-binding is skipped for non-static. Building node-slot under kind=="container" silently inherits all of that. Decide must choose: a NEW kind value (e.g. "node"/"ssr") giving the static spine a clean third arm, vs repurposing "container" + ripping out the legacy plane. This turns on whether any container Site is live in prod (verify #3).
  • The exec-isolation GATE. Two backlog tasks (site-spawner-backlog-ssr-target, site-spawner-backlog-build-isolation) both say "Do NOT start until the connectors D10 exec-isolation fork closes with cold-start numbers." The direction proposes to OVERRIDE with scoped systemd hardening this wave + defer full multi-tenant sandboxing. This must be a NAMED Decide decision (accept scoped mitigation vs honor the block), not a silent override — a node SSR process runs tenant code at REQUEST time continuously, a materially larger trust surface than static's build-time-only model.
  • Port schema. sites.port is a single column — cannot hold both slots' ports simultaneously, which a warm-standby rollback needs. Decide: add a second port field / per-slot table, OR a deterministic per-(site,slot) formula (site-index×2 + slot bit into 7001-7999) that needs no persisted state and is crash-recoverable.

Verify plan (in flight — 7 assignments, RUN-proofs where the claim is load-bearing)

This is the LAST look before the plan is cut. Each assignment names what it will RUN as proof (distrust vacuous green).

  1. next-standalone-empirical (opus, worktree) — Build a realistic next-starter-shaped app (output:standalone + @barkpark/core fetch + bp-* SSR markers) with a GENUINE npm ci in an isolated non-pnpm dir. RUN: build → du -sh standalone node_modules → PORT=<p> node server.js → curl for the markers → measure RSS + boot-to-first-200. Settles STAGE artifact size, HEALTH timeout anchor, per-slot density RSS.
  2. d40-empty-fail-mode (opus) — RUN: curl guerrilla's query endpoint for a doc_type with zero published docs (404 vs 200+[]) AND a node script calling .docs(type).findOne() via @barkpark/core. Proves whether a Next SSR flagship 500s per-request on empty content → whether D40 must be fixed this wave.
  3. guerrilla-site-reality (sonnet) — RUN ssh: count Sites + their kinds (any live kind=container?), is dockerd installed, is barkpark-runtime/builder running, what's bound in 7001-7999 now. Sizes the kind-naming backward-compat risk + confirms Path A is dead on-box.
  4. systemd-node-unit-proof (sonnet) — On guerrilla, RUN systemd-analyze verify on a candidate generic barkpark-site@.service (EnvironmentFile-driven ExecStart=node server.js, MemoryMax/CPUQuota, non-hyphen %i delimiter) + a throwaway systemctl start of a trivial node one-liner to prove the template boots and the caps apply.
  5. caddy-siteflip-proof (sonnet, worktree) — Construct a multi-site Caddyfile with per-site reverse_proxy blocks; sed-flip ONLY site A's port; RUN caddy validate before+after and confirm site B untouched. Proves the site-scoped port-flip SWITCH + validate-or-revert as a third Caddy writer.
  6. kind-seam-and-port-schema (opus) — PROVE the minimal-diff insertion point: RUN the existing deploy_request validation test to confirm unknown-key rejection actually fires (a runtime_target field must mirror that closed-enum discipline); confirm the router branch + content-binding are kind-gated; confirm sites.port is a single column (schema read → migration-or-formula call).
  7. ci-inherited-red (sonnet) — RUN gh run to confirm chat_live.ex:377 doc-gates red is on main HEAD not a slice diff; RUN the specific suspected-flaky Elixir tests locally (targeted mix test, no full suite/OOM) to confirm QueueTest/StudioLiveSheetPresence flake and settle OrgRequireMfa (unconfirmed); confirm cloud.yml's two blocking gates.

Wave log — Digest (2026-07-15): 18 surveyor reports folded. Fork settled by evidence toward Path B (systemd node-slot sibling), Path A harvested for logic only. Four tensions handed to Decide: D40 SSR fail-mode, the "container" name collision, the exec-isolation gate override, the port schema. 7-assignment verify fleet dispatched (RUN-proofs on Next standalone, D40 empty-query, guerrilla reality, systemd template, Caddy site-flip, the dispatch seam, CI reds). NEXT: verifiers report to their own tasks; Decide folds them, opens D61+, files slices.

Decide (2026-07-15) — decisions D61–D72, verification folded, wave in flight

Verification results (RUN-proofs > facts > prose)

  • Next standalone empirical (PROVEN, one assumption OVERTURNED) — a real next build --output:standalone + boot on same-arch arm64: standalone release = 18M (du: 18M .next/standalone, traced node_modules 17M vs 301M full install) — REFUTES the survey's "node_modules ~0B pnpm artifact" AND the pessimistic 137M. Per-process RSS 65MB idle → 85MB under 200 reqs (at/below the 80-150MB assumption). Boot-to-first-200 ~1.5s despite Next logging "✓ Ready in 0ms" — HEALTH must poll the port, not trust the log. CRITICAL: markers reflect the deploy ONLY with export const dynamic='force-dynamic' (a default page served the BUILD-time BUILD_ID; force-dynamic served the injected boot env bp-build-id content="deploy-9f3a" and per-request timestamps differed = true SSR). STAGE must copy THREE pieces (standalone bundles neither static nor public). Next 16 Turbopack HARD-FAILS a CommonJS config against ESM source → template MUST be type:module + next.config.mjs.
  • D40 empty fail-mode (BOTH surveyors right about DIFFERENT cases) — RUN live on guerrilla: a PUBLIC schema with zero matching docs returns HTTP 200 empty (task?filter[status][eq]=zzzznope → {count:0, documents:[]}) → .findOne() null, SAFE (Branch 1). A MISSING or private-anon schema returns HTTP 404 (definitely_nonexistent_type_xyz → 404, weapon anon → 404) → .find()/.findOne() THROW uncaught (Branch 2). The astro/next default post is Branch 2 on guerrilla TODAY (production/post → 404; paper → 200 count 100). So the digest's "findOne mis-returns on empty content" is corrected: only a missing/private SCHEMA 404s. Fix = catch-in-page + pin the proof to paper (D72), NOT patch-core.
  • guerrilla/CP site reality (all three facts settled, one premise corrected) — the sites table lives on barkpark-cp (178.105.92.191, cloud-db-1), NOT guerrilla (content API only). 5 sites, ALL kind=static/framework=astro; ZERO kind=container despite kind defaulting to container — so a new kind='node' value has zero migration/reclassification risk. Path A dead on BOTH boxes (no runtime/builder/waker unit or process; dockerd on cp runs only the CP's own blue/green). Ports 7001-7999 free on both hosts. internal/runtime has exactly one importer (its own main.go).
  • systemd node-unit (PROVEN on guerrilla, hazard surfaced+solved) — a generic bp-node-probe@%i template booted, enforced MemoryMax=200M + CPUQuota=50% (live in systemctl show), and a hyphenated slug my-blog__green survived %i verbatim (systemd does NOT split %i). HAZARD: /root/.asdf/shims/node FAILS exit 126 "No version is set" — must resolve the REAL binary via a stable /usr/local/bin/barkpark-node symlink (the barkpark-connectors.service pattern via asdf where nodejs). Zero CPUQuota/hardening precedent in any shipped unit (all bare User=root) — D70 introduces it.
  • Caddy site-flip (core CONFIRMED, two corrections) — a site-ANCHORED sed flip is surgical (only the target line changes; siblings byte-identical; caddy validate passes before+after). BUT (1) caddy validate is SYNTAX-ONLY — it accepted reverse_proxy not a port!! and even a bare reverse_proxy; the real fail-closed net is the PRE-flip HEALTH probe. (2) instance-deploy.sh's global whole-file sed silently rewrote BOTH sites when they shared a port literal (validate still "Valid") — REJECTED as the multi-site model; extend arm_caddy_site_route's marker anchor to REPLACE-in-place.
  • kind-seam & port-schema (all three sub-claims hold) — DeployRequest.validate_mode/1 is a closed literal match, never String.to_atom (proven by deploy_runner_test.exs 31/0; the file the MUST-RUN named, deploy_request_test.exs, does NOT exist). Cloud branches on kind=="static" at THREE choke points (deploy route l.4745, require_content_binding l.8655, rollback l.4897) — a node arm must be ADDED at each. sites.port is a SINGLE integer column → warm-standby needs a second field/formula. framework is already on the wire (deploy.ex:296) but the box DROPS it — extend DeployRequest.new.
  • CI inherited red (confirmed, one framing corrected) — doc-gates is red on main HEAD itself (chat_live.ex:377 hand-built Studio URL, a parallel session's, headSha confirmed ancestor of origin/main). StudioLiveSheetPresenceTest genuinely flakes (2/3 on assert frame_ms < 10). QueueTest/OrgRequireMfa did NOT reproduce locally (treat as CI-env flakes, not settled-clean). cloud.yml has TWO blocking jobs (compile+format, test) with no continue-on-error — but main has NO GitHub branch protection, so "gates" = review discipline. Any doc-gates/elixir red on a slice must be diffed against main's own run.

Decisions (each mirrors the charter; the charter is the epic's memory)

  • D61 — Runtime target = Path B (systemd node-slot SIBLING deploy/site-deploy-node.sh + shared deploy/lib/site-deploy-common.sh); Path A (Go Docker runtime) DEAD on both boxes, harvested for logic only. Why: Docker cuts against standalone-first + reopens the build-image dependency; the sibling reuses everything W4/W5 proved.
  • D62 — New kind='node' (NOT repurpose "container"); a node arm at all three kind-gated choke points; content-binding REQUIRED for node. Why: zero container rows in prod → zero migration risk; the container default routes to the dead builder + no-content + no-rollback.
  • D63 — Box DeployRequest.runtime_target closed-enum (static|node) mirroring validate_mode; DeployRunner.command_for/2 dispatches to the node script; cloud maps kind→runtime_target on the wire (framework already sent, no longer dropped). Why: the wire seam is live-but-dropped; the discipline is proven.
  • D64 — STAGE = Next standalone THREE-piece copy into immutable releases/<build_id>/ (INVERTS D8); boot PORT=<p> HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 node server.js loopback-bound. Why: the 18M standalone IS the artifact; node_modules must travel with it.
  • D65 — HEALTH = boot-in-place-then-gate on the live process's own port; assert bp-* markers BY VALUE; ≥10s poll deadline; exit 14; on fail stop the just-booted slot, never touch live/Caddy. Why: both process precedents boot-in-place; a throwaway probe doubles footprint.
  • D66 — SWITCH = marker-anchored per-site Caddy port RE-FLIP (extend arm_caddy_site_route to replace-in-place) under with_caddy_lock→backup→validate→reload→revert; REJECT the global sed. Pre-flip HEALTH is the fail-closed net. Why: a node upstream is a port; validate is syntax-only.
  • D67 — Rollback = 2-tier warm-standby: 1 warm previous slot (true <1s Caddy-flip), older cold. RETIRE stops slots beyond current+1-warm. Why: immutable per-build releases make the previous process safe to keep warm; RAM is the price.
  • D68 — Port allocation = sites.port_base int column (migration), lowest-free EVEN base in [7002,7998] scanned from Postgres, blue=base/green=base+1; sites.port stays the live serving port. Why: single column can't express both warm slots; deterministic + Postgres-sourced (the state the Go allocator's always-empty buildState lacked).
  • D69 — Generic barkpark-site@.service, EnvironmentFile-driven, %i=<slug>__<slot>, ExecStart = resolved /usr/local/bin/barkpark-node symlink (NEVER the shim/version-path). Why: one Elixir-coupled precedent; the shim trap (exit 126) is real and already solved on-box.
  • D70 — Scoped systemd hardening THIS wave (MemoryMax/CPUQuota/NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ProtectHome/PrivateTmp); full exec-isolation DEFERRED — a NAMED override of the "do NOT start until connectors D10" gate. Why: bound the new request-time surface now; don't block the whole runtime target on a cross-epic fork.
  • D71 — next-starter: ESM-clean standalone, force-dynamic markers, @barkpark/nextjs request-time SSR fetch, serverToken from slot env. Why: the flagship; empirically the standalone + force-dynamic + loopback shape is exactly the per-slot boot.
  • D72 — D40 for SSR = CATCH-IN-PAGE (Branch-2 404), NOT patch-core; pin the proof to paper. Why: only a missing/private schema 404s; swallowing in core would hide misconfig from every consumer.

Wave plan — 6 slices in flight (task id · surface · builder · gate)

  1. site-spawner-w7-next-starter · templates/ · fable · [D71,D72] — ESM standalone Next 16, force-dynamic bp-* markers, request-time SSR fetch, catch-in-page. Gate: cd templates/next-starter && npm ci && npm run build && test -f .next/standalone/server.js + a boot-marker smoke.
  2. site-spawner-w7-node-deploy-engine · deploy/ · fable · [D61,D63-D69] — site-deploy-node.sh 6-stage engine + lib/site-deploy-common.sh + barkpark-site@.service + density doctrine. Gate: bash deploy/site-deploy-node.sh --self-test && bash deploy/site-deploy.sh --self-test && shellcheck deploy/site-deploy-node.sh deploy/lib/site-deploy-common.sh deploy/site-deploy.sh.
  3. site-spawner-w7-cloud-node-kind · cloud/ · fable · [D62,D66-D68] — kind=node third router arm + framework legality + port_base migration & allocator + runtime_target on the wire. Gate: cd cloud && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark_cloud/registry/site_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/web/router_sites_test.exs test/barkpark_cloud/sites/node_port_allocator_test.exs + compile-warnings-as-errors + format.
  4. site-spawner-w7-box-dispatch · api/ · opus · [D62,D63,D71] — DeployRequest.runtime_target + DeployRunner.command_for/2 dispatch + Provisioner framework-keyed template. Gate: cd api && CC=clang mix test test/barkpark/sites/deploy_runner_test.exs test/barkpark/sites/provisioner_test.exs.
  5. site-spawner-w7-cli · internal/cli + internal/cloudclient · opus · [D62] — --kind node create + node rollback narration (fix the static-only symlink copy) + cloudclient port/runtime_target fields. Gate: CC=clang go build ./... && go vet ./internal/cli/... && go test ./internal/cli/....
  6. site-spawner-w7-node-live-proof · deploy/ · opus · [all] — site-spawner-node-live-proof.sh: spawn → 6 stages drive a running node process → live SSR URL with markers → <1s warm-slot rollback. Gate: bash deploy/site-spawner-node-live-proof.sh --self-check && shellcheck deploy/site-spawner-node-live-proof.sh + a merge-gated LIVE guerrilla walk (lead).

Integration order: next-starter + node-deploy-engine + cloud-node-kind + box-dispatch are the spine (file-disjoint, parallel); cli threads the decided contract in parallel; live-proof is written in parallel and RUN live by the lead after 1-5 merge and guerrilla redeploys. Backlog filed: site-spawner-backlog-nuxt-sveltekit, site-spawner-backlog-node-exec-isolation, site-spawner-backlog-node-scale-to-zero, site-spawner-backlog-core-list-404-swallow.

Wave log — Decide (2026-07-15): 7 verifiers folded; central fork SETTLED toward Path B (Path A dead on both boxes), pessimistic assumptions REFUTED (18M/85MB/1.5s), D40 SSR danger reframed as a missing/private-schema 404. D61–D72 opened + committed to the charter. Six slices filed + published + read-back-verified (parented, paper-linked, rubric-quality); four backlog children filed. NEXT: builders claim their task, build in worktrees, stamp evidence, gate; the lead runs the live guerrilla proof post-merge.

Review debrief (2026-07-15) — wave built, reviewed, graded A-

Reviewer: one Fable, last hands before merge, own worktree. Reviewed every green slice's full diff, fixed issues in place on -r branches, re-ran gates. All six slices BUILT and green; the LIVE guerrilla capstone is merge-gated (lead runs it). Grade: A- as it will merge.

What shipped — per slice (final branch · verdict)

  • site-spawner-w7-next-starter → loop-epic/w7-next-starter-templates-next-starter-e-0-r. The flagship Next 16 ESM standalone adapter: force-dynamic markers reflect the runtime boot env, request-time content fetch via @barkpark/nextjs, D40 catch-in-page honest-empty, default doc_type=paper. Reviewer fix: baked a sixth marker bp-render-ts (a request-scoped Date.now()) — the true-SSR proof the live-proof asserts by default and which the five original markers (all boot- or content-stable) could not provide. Verified live: npm run build green (route still ƒ Dynamic, STANDALONE_OK) and a boot-smoke showed bp-render-ts DIFFERS across two requests while the other five markers serve, and an anon guerrilla read returned a real doc. Gate green.
  • site-spawner-w7-node-deploy-engine → loop-epic/w7-node-deploy-engine-deploy-site-deploy-1-r. The node-slot SSR engine: shared common lib (emit/BPSTAGE/meta_value/caddy-lock extracted, static engine still 80/80), the six stages over a running process, marker-value HEALTH boot-in-place, marker-anchored per-site Caddy port flip (never the global sed), warm-standby retire + <1s rollback, the barkpark-site@ hardened slot unit, density doctrine. Reviewer fix (real bug): the HEALTH probe hits the raw node port directly, bypassing Caddy; Caddy arms with handle_path /sites/<slug>/* (STRIPS the prefix) and next-starter has no basePath, so the node process serves the marker page at ROOT — but the engine defaulted BARKPARK_SITE_HEALTH_PATH to /sites/<slug>/, which 404s on the raw port → a GOOD build would fail HEALTH (exit 14) on the live box. The self-test masked it by always overriding the path to /. Default is now /; the main self-test deploy exercises that default (override removed, so the fix is non-vacuous). Gate green (58/58 node, 80/80 static, shellcheck clean).
  • site-spawner-w7-cloud-node-kind → loop-epic/w7-cloud-node-kind-kind-node-third-route-2-r. kind=node third router arm at all three choke points (deploy drives the same 6-stage machine, content-binding required, rollback not-422'd), framework legality, port_base migration + lowest-free-even NodePortAllocator, deploy_payload emits runtime_target + idle-slot target_port. Reviewer fix (cross-slice honesty): the rollback route did NOT emit runtime_target, so the CLI (which resolves a rollback target by id only, with no kind) narrated a node rollback as an "atomic symlink swap" — a lie for the flagship node capability, whose rollback is a Caddy upstream flip. Now the rollback envelope carries runtime_target (node|static) mapped from kind; the node-rollback test pins it. Builder-proven gate 94/0 (cloud has no local deps/DB here — not re-runnable in the review worktree; my edits are a one-line map value + a partial-assertion test, both low-risk; the lead's Cloud CI is the gate).
  • site-spawner-w7-box-dispatch → loop-epic/w7-box-dispatch-deployrequest-runtime-ta-3 (no reviewer changes). DeployRequest.runtime_target closed-enum validator (never String.to_atom on request data), DeployRunner.command_for/2 dispatches the node engine script, Provisioner selects next-starter for :node. Non-vacuous tests (stub scripts echo STATIC_DEPLOY_RAN/NODE_DEPLOY_RAN + argv proof + closed-enum rejection). Builder-proven gate; api has no local deps in the review worktree.
  • site-spawner-w7-cli → loop-epic/w7-cli-bp-cloud-site-create-kind-node-no-4 (no reviewer changes). --kind node, node runtime narration on create/status, rollback mechanism branched by runtime_target, cloudclient carries runtime_target/port/port_base so -o json stops silently dropping them. Gate re-run GREEN in the review worktree (CC=clang go build/vet/test + gofmt clean). RuntimeTargetIsNode matches both "node" and "node-slot", so it is compatible with the CP's "node" value my cloud fix emits.
  • site-spawner-w7-node-live-proof → loop-epic/w7-node-live-proof-deploy-site-spawner-n-5 (no reviewer changes). The capstone harness: same six stages drive a systemd slot to a live SSR URL, markers by value, per-request SSR (bp-render-ts differs), warm-slot rollback <1s, fail-closed (a failed-HEALTH slot never takes the upstream). Offline --self-check drives all 39 named reds. Gate re-run GREEN (self-check + shellcheck).

Cross-slice coherence — three contract gaps found and CLOSED

  1. HEALTH path vs Caddy strip vs no basePath — the engine probed the sub-path; the process serves root. Fixed in the engine (default /).
  2. Rollback narration — the CLI branched on an envelope field the CP never sent. Fixed in the CP (emit runtime_target on rollback).
  3. SSR proof marker — the live-proof asserted bp-render-ts that next-starter did not bake. Fixed in next-starter (bake it), live-verified.

These three were the difference between a green offline suite and a green LIVE walk: each would have false-RED'd or lied on guerrilla. All now consistent (marker names, runtime_target values, probe path).

What the lead MUST know before / after merge

  • Merge order: box-dispatch + cloud-node-kind are .ex/.exs → WAIT for the Elixir Test gate (per the "don't merge before Elixir Test" law). CLI (Go) and the two deploy/bash slices merge on their own gates. next-starter is templates-only (watch TestEmbeddedCatalog if the embedded catalog flags drift).
  • LIVE-walk dependency NOT built this wave (blocks a fully-green capstone): the live-proof reads deployment.slot, deployment.port, and deployment.health_exit_code from the deploy/status JSON. NO W7 slice surfaces those in the CP's CLI-facing deployment JSON (the cloud slice added port_base to site_json and runtime_target/target_port to the box PAYLOAD only). On guerrilla these degrade to false-REDS (DEPLOY_NO_SLOT etc.), never vacuous greens — the harness stays honest — but the six-stage LIVE assertions on slot/port/health-exit will not go green until a follow-up slice surfaces them. Filed site-spawner-backlog-node-deployment-slot-surfacing (P1). The lead should either land that surfacing before the live walk or accept the slot/port assertions degrading.
  • Merge-gated criteria the lead closes on merge: next-starter c5, node-deploy-engine c6, cloud-node-kind c6, box-dispatch c4, cli c4, node-live-proof c3 (the LIVE guerrilla walk). All six tasks stay lifecycle in_progress with evidence stamped — correct.
  • Known residual risks (accepted, not blockers): port_base has no DB unique constraint (two truly-concurrent node creates could both grab 7002 — brief deferred the constraint); MemoryMax=512M on the slot is a starting guess; ProtectSystem=strict makes the release read-only (SSR-first — Next ISR would need a ReadWritePaths carve-out); the default per-slug cksum port pair can collide (the central allocator is the CP's job and is wired).

Ledger audit

All six slice tasks: lifecycle in_progress, criteria 0..N-1 stamped met with concrete boot-smoke / gate evidence AS BUILT, the final merge-gated criterion left OPEN for the lead — honest and correct. No fabricated done. No task outside this wave was touched. One new backlog child filed (deployment slot/port/health-exit surfacing). No ledger lies to fix. Evidence on next-starter c2/c3 says "five markers" where there are now six after my fix — a harmless understatement, not a lie, left as-is.

Grade: A- (Cody mandate — honest commentary)

Genuinely strong: the engine is a faithful sibling of the proven static machine — the shared common lib means the two cannot drift on the wire protocol, the marker reader, or the one Caddyfile lock, and the marker-anchored per-site port flip correctly refuses the global-sed corruption the static engine was RUN-proven to suffer. HEALTH is content-truth (bp-build-id == this build BY VALUE) and boot-in-place, fail-closed throughout (a lying/broken slot is purged and never takes the upstream, live-proven in the self-test). The next-starter is a real Next 16 ESM standalone app whose markers reflect the RUNTIME boot env, proven against live guerrilla content. The closed-enum runtime_target validator keeps command/unit-injection out of argv. Tests are non-vacuous across all surfaces.

What falls short of A/A+: the wish's literal finish line — a live 6-stage walk on guerrilla driving a real node process to an SSR URL + <1s warm rollback — is NOT demonstrated this session (same merge-gate as W4/W5), AND unlike those it carries an unbuilt dependency: the deployment JSON does not yet surface slot/port/health_exit_code, so even post-merge the live-proof's slot-level assertions degrade until a follow-up lands. Three real cross-slice contract breaks (health path, rollback field, SSR marker) shipped from the builders and had to be caught here — they would each have broken the live walk — which is why this is A- and not A: the slices were individually excellent but did not fully reconcile their shared contract. Nothing is bloated; the density doctrine and resource caps are honestly documented.

Next wave

Land site-spawner-backlog-node-deployment-slot-surfacing (surface deployment.slot/port/health_exit_code in the CP CLI-facing JSON) so the live-proof's slot assertions can go green, then run the guerrilla live walk. After that: the central per-site port allocator with a DB unique constraint (close the concurrent-create race), and the second/third container frameworks (nuxt/sveltekit) on the SAME node-slot engine to prove the adapter axis generalizes. Node exec-isolation (tenant SSR code runs at request time now, not just build time) is the real crux the density/hardening doctrine only begins to address — site-spawner-backlog-node-exec-isolation.
description: Wave-7 strategy for the Barkpark Cloud site-spawner epic: unlock the second runtime target (node-slot SSR) so container frameworks — Next.js first — run via the same proven 6-stage deploy state machine. Sets the direction (Path B systemd node-slot over Path A Docker), the choices leaned toward, and an 18-question survey plan to settle the process-lifecycle crux.

tags.rationale: Wave 7 of the co-located site-spawner epic — the second runtime target that unlocks all container frameworks.
The wave delivers a per-site long-running Node SSR process (next start / node server.js) driven by the deploy machine.
This paper is the Strategize-phase living story: direction plus the survey fleet before Digest.

title: Site Spawner Wave 7 — the node-slot SSR runtime target
